subject: Saturday's biggest story was a repost with nothing behind it
summary: A repost from the president, a new Tesla driving release, a rough week for AI stocks and a record game launch shared a loud Saturday.

lead.head: Trump reposts a health care card, then the White House says no
text: The day's largest story was a repost, and the interesting part is who made the offer. Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed put out a card proposing to put the president's name on Medicare for All. The president reposted it with no comment. The White House then rejected the idea.
The post that carried it reached {views} readers, and the reply from El-Sayed himself drew a large audience of its own. That is a lot of attention for a story with no policy in it yet.
A repost costs nothing and commits to nothing. That is why it travels so well, and why rejecting it later is easy too.

notes.head: Tesla starts sending FSD v15 to a first group of cars
notes.text: Tesla says its driver-assist software has a new vision system and is going to a first group of owners. The safety claims are Tesla's own, and the record holds no outside test of them. Tesla's post drew the biggest audience, and Elon Musk added his own. Until someone other than the company measures it, treat this as a release note.

notes.head: AI stocks keep sliding into a correction
notes.text: The S&P 500 and the Dow are in a correction and the Nasdaq has given back its gain for the year. Chip markets in Asia fell hard first and Wall Street followed, and Bitcoin dropped too. Anthropic's newly listed shares were among the ones that fell. The pattern is that AI names moved together on the way up and are moving together on the way down.

notes.head: Take-Two says GTA VI took in a record first day
notes.text: Take-Two reports {sales} in the first day and calls it the biggest entertainment launch ever. The catch is in the counting. The figure includes months of pre-orders, and an outside estimate the day before was about half as large. The company chose a flattering definition of a day.

text: Saturday's pattern is that the biggest numbers came from the easiest things to share. A repost, a release note and a launch total each drew huge audiences while saying little that can be checked.
My call is that the AI selloff is the one to follow, because it is the only story here with a price that anyone can check tomorrow.

views.of: views on the post that carried the repost

sales.of: Take-Two's reported first-day sales of GTA VI
